title: The Little Bird and the Hands of Destiny
snippet: A small story, perhaps familiar to many, yet one that carries a profound truth about life, compassion, and the mysterious hands of destiny...
content:
[CENTER]*A small story carrying an eternal truth*

A small story, perhaps familiar to many, yet one that carries a profound truth about life and destiny.

I happened to hear this story in one of the videos that appeared during our usual pastime of scrolling through social media. Something about it stayed with me. Out of curiosity, I searched for more, only to come across different versions of the same story. Though the narrations varied slightly, the central message remained unchanged.

I am not attempting to create another version or add anything new to it. I simply wish to retell the story, preserving its essence and the beautiful message it conveys.

It is the story of a little bird, one among the countless creations of this universe, whose life was already destined to unfold in a particular way.

Once, Lord Vishnu visited Lord Shiva at Mount Kailash. Garuda, the divine eagle and vehicle of Lord Vishnu, waited outside while the two deities met.

As Garuda stood waiting, he noticed a little bird sitting nearby on a branch. He admired its tiny form and fragile existence.

Just then, Yama Dharmaraja, the Lord of Death and Justice, arrived at Mount Kailash. Perhaps he too had an appointment with Lord Shiva.

As Yama passed by the little bird, he glanced at it with an expression of surprise and puzzlement.

Garuda noticed that unusual glance. The little bird, too, seemed frightened by Yama's presence.

Assuming that Yama's glance carried an indication of impending danger, Garuda's compassionate heart could not bear the thought of the little creature meeting its end.

Without a moment's hesitation, he decided to save it.

With his mighty wings and incredible speed, Garuda carried the little bird thousands of miles away, crossing oceans and reaching a distant forest. There, he gently placed it on the branch of a large tree, believing that he had secured its safety.

Satisfied with his timely intervention, Garuda swiftly returned to Mount Kailash.

When Yama Dharmaraja came out, he was once again surprised to find that the little bird was no longer there.

Garuda, feeling proud of his act of compassion, explained how he had carried the little creature far away to protect it from whatever danger Yama's glance might have indicated.

Yama listened and smiled.

He then revealed the reason behind his earlier expression of surprise.

The little bird's lifespan was nearing its end. According to its destiny, it was meant to be bitten by a poisonous snake hiding in a hollow in a tree branch, in a distant forest thousands of miles away, across the oceans.

Yama had wondered how such a tiny bird could possibly reach that distant place in the short time left to it.

And there it was!

Garuda, in his attempt to save the little bird, had unknowingly carried it to the very place where its destiny awaited.

What an irony!

Garuda believed he was changing the little bird's destiny, while unknowingly becoming the very instrument through which that destiny unfolded.

Perhaps this is one of the profound mysteries of life. The story is already written, and every path we take may lead us towards that one inevitable destination. We make choices, change directions, overcome obstacles and sometimes go to great lengths to alter the course of events. Yet, there may be things beyond our understanding and control.

Does that mean we should simply surrender to destiny and let life unfold?

Not necessarily.

Perhaps the wisdom lies in accepting what is beyond our control while taking responsibility for what is within our reach. We may not know where every path leads, but we can certainly choose how we walk it.

Let us be wise enough to live each moment to its fullest, make the best of what we have, and walk our chosen path with awareness, compassion and grace.

For we may not have the power to rewrite the story, but we can make every moment of our part in it meaningful.

Some stories do not need elaborate explanations. They simply leave us with a thought, allowing us to look at life a little differently.

And perhaps, this is one such story.
